inlines.v: OUT'LAW, noun A person excluded from the benefit of the law, or deprived of its protection. Formerly any person might kill an outlaw; but it is now held unlawful for any person to put to death an outlaw except the sheriff, who has a warrant for that purpose. OUT'LAW, verb transitive To deprive of the benefit and protection of law; to proscribe.
